title: metastable-cache-oscillation-investigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a production capacity event on 2025-11-14 we observed repeated, self- amplifying KV cache eviction waves that produced cross-tenant latency spikes and transient OOM pressure on a subset of serving instances. This ticket tracks the investigation into a metastable cache oscillation hypothesis, the short-term containment actions taken, and the medium-term hardening work required to prevent recurrence.

Scope: Affects Redwood hosted inference nodes in us-east-1 serving mixed-tenant traffic under bursty prefix distributions. The behavior manifests as alternating high-eviction periods followed by aggressive re-population (write amplification) causing slab churn, garbage, and elevated 95/99 latency for token generation.

Impact: Several high-throughput product customers experienced 95th percentile latency regressions (200-400ms increase) for 6–18 minute windows; one customer reported retry amplification in their orchestration layer. No data loss; no authentication or authorization issues.

Hypothesis: A combination of skewed tenant key distributions, an eviction priority jitter in the slab allocator, and a KV eviction scoring decay bug lead to synchronized eviction-repopulate cycles across co-located tenants. This synchronization produces a positive feedback loop that amplifies memory pressure and stalls IO paths, causing cascading latency degradation.
comments: 2025-11-15 — Asha Patel: Initial incident triage. Isolated affected shard ring and activated emergency throttles for noisy tenants. Opened this investigation ticket to coordinate root cause work and mitigations.

2025-11-15 — Ethan Zhao: Captured heap profiles and eviction traces. Observed correlated eviction timestamps across tenant namespaces indicating synchronous windowing. Attached Grafana panels and flamegraphs in links.

2025-11-16 — Priya Nair (SRE): Deployed temporary eviction pacing (rate limiter) and increased per-tenant soft caps; latency returned to baseline within 8 minutes for most customers. Noted two tenants continued to cause repeated oscillation when soft cap reached.

2025-11-17 — Miguel Torres (Runtime Eng): Identified a regression introduced in runtime-1.20 where eviction-score decay constants were changed to improve throughput; this inadvertently made eviction priority converge faster for many keys leading to synchronized evictions under bursty loads.

2025-11-18 — Design Review with Product: Decided to prioritize gradual rollout of a guarded decay constant rollback and implement additional guardrails to avoid tenant synchronization rather than an immediate global rollback.
2025-11-19 — Security: Confirmed no data exposure. No security review required for the immediate fixes, but telemetry changes will have an access-controlled dashboard.

2025-11-20 — Ethan Zhao: Prepared PR with three components: (1) decay constant rollback with feature flag; (2) tenant-scoped eviction jitter to break synchronization; (3) new slab-occupancy alert with auto-throttle trigger. PR link in 'links' field.
decision_notes: Short-term: enable feature-flagged rollback of decay constants and deploy tenant-scoped eviction pacing to affected rings. Medium-term: introduce random jitter to eviction timing, enhance tenant isolation metrics, and add a runbook automation to soft-throttle noisy tenants automatically. Long-term: redesign eviction scoring to include per-tenant entropy and implement canary ramping for scoring changes. We will keep the rollback feature-flagged for staggered rollout and telemetry validation.
next_steps: Ethan Zhao — Merge and canary PR to 10% of serving rings behind feature flag (target: 2025-11-22).
Priya Nair (SRE) — Add slab-occupancy alert with auto-throttle action and escalation policy (target: 2025-11-24).
Miguel Torres — Implement eviction-timing jitter (unit-tested simulation + perf bench) and measure impact on throughput (target: 2025-12-05).
Asha Patel — Coordinate customer communications for affected accounts and follow up on retry amplification reports (target: 2025-11-21).
Reliability — Draft regression test harness that reproduces synchronized eviction cycles in CI using traffic replay (target: 2025-12-12).
